notes: Access: direct curl_cffi (impersonate chrome124) to www.frontgate.com, 200 OK throughout, no block encountered. Counts from the site's own Unbxd API proxy (UnbxdAPI?categoryId=<id>...) -> numberOfProducts, double-verified with a boundary test (unbxdStart=N-1 -> 1 item, unbxdStart=N -> 0 items) for every row below (all matched exactly; the single 1-item row, Outdoor Entertaining Clearance, could not be boundary-tested the same way because Unbxd ignores 'start' entirely below its page size for a 1-result set, so numberOfProducts=1 was instead cross-checked by re-querying 4 times with different start offsets, all returning the same single product consistently). Discovery: pulled the site's own full nav/category JSON tree (/JSONAPIs?module=categories, ~1600 nodes) and located Frontgate's entire Sale/Outlet/Clearance tree. The company is indeed an HSN/QVC-group site with an explicit 'Outlet' section as the task flagged: the top nav node whose OWN categoryTitle is literally 'Clearance' (categoryId 98147, URL /sale/) contains a child also titled 'Clearance' (categoryId 98150, URL /sale/outlet/) - this passes the Sale-vs-Clearance test cleanly since the site's own taxonomy label is 'Clearance', not a generic 'Sale/Deals/Offers' name, even though the URL slug happens to be /sale/. Below 98150 sit two structurally different lists that turned out to be numeric ALIASES of the same master pool: 'Clearance'(98150, /sale/outlet/) and 'All Clearance'(211154, /sale/outlet/view-all/) both report numberOfProducts=268 - kept the canonical visible-in-nav node (98150) as the master Clearance row and did NOT duplicate 211154 (its child department tiles are hidden-from-nav river tiles pointing at the same 268-item pool, not separate assortments). All named department-level clearance sub-listings (Outdoor Furniture, Outdoor Decor & Pool, Furniture, Bed & Bath [+ its Bath/Bed children], Lighting & Decor, Rugs & Pillows, Tabletop & Entertaining [+ its Serveware/Outdoor Entertaining children], Holiday Decor & Gifts, Clearance Under $100, and 'New to Clearance' which despite its /sale/outlet/new-arrivals/ URL slug is a recently-marked-down-to-clearance filter INSIDE the Clearance tree, not the site's separate New Arrivals concept - kept here, excluded from the New Arrivals file) are real, non-empty, distinct product-count listings kept as leaf rows under the Clearance parent. DROPPED as zero-product (site itself returns numberOfProducts=0): 'Tabletop Clearance' (categoryId 221202) and 'Bar & Wine Clearance' (categoryId 221203) under the Tabletop & Entertaining Clearance branch, and three legacy alternate-path clearance URLs discovered elsewhere in the tree that are effectively dead/depopulated (Outdoor Furniture Clearance at /outdoor/outdoor-savings/ catId 194170, Outdoor Decor & Pool Clearance at /outdoor/outdoor-decor-savings/ catId 220184, and Holiday Clearance at /holiday-decor/special-savings/ catId 89178 - all return numberOfProducts=0 despite appearing as live nav-visible nodes; they look like older duplicate entry points for the same content now reachable canonically via /sale/outlet/*, so nothing was lost by dropping them). AMBIGUOUS: 'Limited Time Only' (categoryId 197154, /sale/limited-time-only/, numberOfProducts=260) is a direct sibling of the 'Clearance' node under the same top-level 'Clearance'/sale hub, and is a real, large, non-empty product listing - but its own category title is 'Limited Time Only', not Clearance/Outlet/Final Sale/Last Chance, and its MULTI_LEVEL_TEMPLATE_CATEGORY attribute reads like a time-boxed promotional sale filter rather than a permanent-markdown outlet listing. Recorded per the brief's guidance rather than guessed either way; flagged for manual review. EXCLUDED outright (not recorded): 'Free Shipping' (categoryId 251654, /sale/free-shipping/) and its Bedding/Outdoor-Sets children - a shipping-perk filter, no markdown/clearance signal at all.
